# Catudvārajātaka (Ja 439)

**ID:** Ja 439  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Catudvārajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In this Pali version, the Bodhisatta is not Mittavinda but appears separately as a deity (*devaputta* / *devarājā*) who observes his suffering [JIABS 2013; Fausböll 1887].

The tale represents an earlier iteration of the narrative cycle shared with the *Losaka Jātaka* (Ja 41) and the Northern Buddhist legend of Maitrakanyaka attested in the *Avadānaśataka* (no. 36), the *Divyāvadāna*, and Kṣemendra's *Avadānakalpalatā* [JIABS 2013; Kudo 2004; Grünwedel 1900]. While later Sanskrit avadānas transform Maitrakanyaka into the Bodhisattva whose suffering sparks universal compassion leading to rebirth in Tuṣita heaven, the Pali Jātaka maintains Mittavinda's separate, unredeemed status [JIABS 2013; Grünwedel 1900]. Elements of the *Catudvāra* and *Losaka* Jātakas are also blended in Kang Senghui's Chinese translation in the *Liudu ji jing* [Huynh 2016].

**Sources**
